reason: Conversation 2 reached the key sensible step: it told the customer to unplug first and clean the hidden sump compartment, which the customer did (finding grey slimy water) and which produced a real improvement, before escalating to an engineer when the light returned. Conversation 1 fixated on a non-existent float inside the water container, never directed the customer to the sump at all, and then jumped to 'level switch or control board' and an engineer, so the homeowner left without the one owner-level fix that actually helped. Conversation 2 loses marks for an inefficient middle section (an irrelevant drum-warmth test the customer rightly challenged, and a drain-hose check requiring rear access it already knew was impossible) and for ending slightly overconfident that the pump needs replacing, but it was honest that it could be blocked versus failed and named no part number.
